rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miracles may violate habitual expectations, but they are not intrinsic impossibilities; only contradictions are rationally impossible, and longstanding rational acceptance confirms this distinction.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الأمور والحوادث وإن أنكرتها العادة واستبعدتها إلا أنها ليست أمورا مستحيلة بالذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miracles do not oppose nature in general: material existence already changes life into death, forms into other forms, and prosperity into adversity and back.
rows.anchor: أن أصل هذه الأمور أعني المعجزات ليس مما تنكره عادة الطبيعة بل هي مما يتعاوره نظام المادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary material causes work gradually under specific spatial and temporal conditions; miracles occur outside those customary conditions, apparently through a willing agent.
rows.anchor: إنما الفرق بين صنع العادة وبين المعجزة الخارقة هو أن الأسباب المادية المشهودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Simple sense experience and current natural science cannot verify miracles, yet science cannot deny extraordinary events that witnesses and published records document.
rows.anchor: وكما أن الحس والتجربة الساذجين لا يساعدان على تصديق هذه الخوارق للعادة كذلك النظر العلمي الطبيعي

rows.speaker: الباحثين في الآثار الروحية من علماء العصر
rows.claim: Modern researchers hypothesize that strenuous spiritual practice gives people control of unknown electromagnetic waves, explaining extraordinary physical actions; a complete theory could unify many phenomena under natural causation.
rows.anchor: الباحثين في الآثار الروحية من علماء العصر أن يعللوه بجريان أمواج مجهولة الكتريسية مغناطيسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A natural effect must have a natural cause if its relation to its cause is itself natural; natural causation consists of material entities joined by particular relations producing a later entity.
rows.anchor: لا معنى لمعلول طبيعي لا علة طبيعية له مع فرض كون الرابطة طبيعية محفوظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an does not identify a final natural cause for ordinary and extraordinary material events, since that is outside its general purpose; it nevertheless affirms a material cause for every event by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: يثبت لكل حادث مادي سببا ماديا بإذن الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted promise says God provides an exit and sustenance for the God-conscious and suffices those who trust Him, even when familiar causes seem to rule this out.
rows.anchor: فإن صدر الآية يحكم بالإطلاق من غير تقييد أن كل من اتقى الله وتوكل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The open-ended promises that God answers supplication and suffices His servant reinforce that ordinary causal expectations do not limit what God brings about.
rows.anchor: كما يدل عليه أيضا إطلاق قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God accomplishes His affair explains the preceding promise’s unrestricted scope; 12:21 states the same unrestricted divine sovereignty.
rows.anchor: ثم الجملة التالية وهي قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He initially considers two accounts of God’s access to an event beyond ordinary means: direct will without a material cause, or an unknown natural cause known to God.
rows.anchor: وهذا يحتمل وجهين أحدهما أن يتوسل تعالى إليه من غير سبب مادي وعلة طبيعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second possible account is that God reaches the intended event through a hidden natural cause unknown to people.
rows.anchor: وثانيهما أن يكون هناك سبب طبيعي مستور عن علمنا يحيط به الله سبحانه

words: قد جعل الله لكل شيء قدرا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decree that God set a measure for everything supports the second account: every effect has a divinely measured set of relations through which God can bring it about despite absent customary causes.
rows.anchor: فإنها تدل على أن كل شيء من المسببات أعم مما تقتضيه الأسباب العادية أو لا تقتضيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This account does not deny causality; it affirms real causal relations among things while holding that God controls and changes them as He wills.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا نفيا للعلية والسببية بين الأشياء بل إثبات أنها بيد الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every material entity is determined through its connections with all material entities that precede and accompany it, and so is caused by another entity.
rows.anchor: ما من موجود مادي إلا وهو متقدر مرتبط بجميع الموجودات المادية التي تتقدمه وتصاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses on divine measure show things descending from undetermined plenitude into particular existence by a determination that precedes and accompanies them, including their relations to other existents.
rows.anchor: تدل على أن الأشياء تنزل من ساحة الإطلاق إلى مرحلة التعين والتشخص بتقدير منه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Qur’an affirms universal creation, an ordered creation, and general causality, material events—customary or miraculous—follow a stable order and arise from a preceding cause.
rows.anchor: أن نظام الوجود في الموجودات المادية سواء كانت على جري العادة أو خارقة لها على صراط مستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Customary causes that sometimes fail to produce their effects are not the true causes; more consistent hidden causes underlie events, a possibility scientific work on germs and extraordinary events may support.
rows.anchor: أن الأسباب العادية التي ربما يقع التخلف بينها وبين مسبباتها ليست بأسباب حقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Qur’an recognizes causes among things, it attributes the whole order to God: causes are not independent, and God alone is the true, complete agent.
rows.anchor: المؤثر الحقيقي بتمام معنى الكلمة ليس إلا الله عز سلطانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns all things and may grant others only a dependent permission to act; delegated possession never makes its recipient independent of Him.
rows.anchor: قل اللهم مالك الملك تؤتي الملك من تشآء وتنزع الملك ممن تشآء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic language of intercession and permission means causes receive their efficacy from God while remaining non-independent agents.
rows.anchor: فالأسباب تملكت السببية بتمليكه تعالى، وهي غير مستقلة في عين أنها مالكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission presupposes a possible impediment blocking an existing productive capacity; hence a cause has a real power to affect its effect, though God governs it.
rows.anchor: فقد بان أن في كل السبب مبدئا مؤثرا مقتضيا للتأثير به يؤثر في مسببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger’s miraculous sign issues from an effective principle in the prophet’s soul, whose operation still depends on God’s permission.
rows.anchor: إتيان الآيات المعجزة من الأنبياء وصدورها عنهم إنما هو لمبدأ مؤثر موجود في نفوسهم الشريفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an acknowledges sorcery in some measure and indicates that it too proceeds from a psychic principle in the sorcerer, subject to permission.
rows.anchor: الآية كما أنها تصدق صحة السحر في الجملة كذلك تدل على أن السحر أيضا كالمعجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miracles, sorcery, saintly wonders, and acquired ascetic feats all arise from psychic principles and volitional powers; prophets’, messengers’, and believers’ principle overcomes every cause.
rows.anchor: جميع الأمور الخارقة للعادة سواء سميت معجزة أو سحرا أو غير ذلك ككرامات الأولياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s unrestricted promises to support messengers and believers show that their victorious principle is beyond nature and above matter.
rows.anchor: هذا المبدأ الموجود المنصور أمر وراء الطبيعة وفوق المادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Material things are limited and lose when opposed by something of higher measure; a divinely supported immaterial prophetic soul can empower a cause to overcome a material obstacle.
rows.anchor: فإن الأمور المادية مقدرة محدودة مغلوبة لما هو فوقها قدرا واحدا عند التزاحم والمغالبة

words: فإذا جاء أمر الله قضي بالحق
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The psychic cause’s effect requires God’s command in addition to permission, by coinciding or uniting with that command.
rows.anchor: تدل على أن تأثير هذا المقتضى يتوقف على أمر من الله تعالى يصاحب الاذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here God’s command is interpreted as the creative word of bringing something into existence, expressed as “Be.”
rows.anchor: وقد فسر الأمر في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human choices and actions depend on God willing that people themselves will; these verses do not mean God wills every desire, which would imply a divine will can fail.
rows.anchor: وليست في مقام بيان أن كل ما يريده الإنسان فقد أراده الله فإنه خطأ فاحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses saying God could have guided or made everyone believe refute the mistaken claim that whatever a person wills is itself willed by God.
rows.anchor: مع أنه خلاف ظواهر الآيات الكثيرة الواردة في هذا المورد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human willing and action are both willed by God, with action proceeding through the person’s own will as an intermediary.
rows.anchor: فإرادتنا ومشيئتنا إذا تحققت فينا فهي مرادة بإرادة الله ومشيئته لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All ordinary and extraordinary events, whether good or evil, depend on natural causes and on God’s will and command.
rows.anchor: مستندة في تحققها إلى أسباب طبيعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic miracles and a servant’s answered prayer also involve a decisive divine will and command, unlike extraordinary events generally considered only under permission.
rows.anchor: إلا أن قسما منها وهو المعجزة من الأنبياء أو ما سأله عبد ربه بالدعاء لا يخلو عن إرادة موجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary events align with customary outward causes and real natural causes; extraordinary events rely on hidden natural causes plus divine permission, while prophetic miracles also have a challenge establishing the mission.
rows.anchor: وأن المعجزة مستندة إلى سبب طبيعي حقيقي بإذن الله وأمره إذا كان هناك تحد يبتنى عليه صحة النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike other causal processes, the causes of miracles and divinely answered prayers are never defeated or overcome.
rows.anchor: أن سببهما لا يصير مغلوبا مقهورا قط بخلاف سائر المسببات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection argues that discovering a miracle’s natural cause would make the event available to anyone and make its evidentiary force depend on people’s knowledge and era.
rows.anchor: لو فرضنا الإحاطة والبلوغ إلى السبب الطبيعي الذي للمعجزة كانت المعجزة ميسورة ممكنة الإتيان لغير النبي أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks what logically connects a miracle with a messenger’s truth, since reason sees no necessary link between truthful teaching about God and an extraordinary act.
rows.anchor: وها هنا سؤال وهو أنه ما هي الرابطة بين المعجزة وبين حقية دعوى الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’anic narratives say prophets were asked for signs and supplied them; some signs came before any request, including those of Moses and Aaron, Jesus, and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: فإنهم على ما يقصه القرآن حينما بثوا دعوتهم سئلوا عن آية تدل على حقية دعواهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view says miracles persuade ordinary people whose reasoning cannot grasp rational truths, while the intellectual elite already have adequate proofs.
rows.anchor: ولذا قيل إن المعجزات لإقناع نفوس العامة لقصور عقولهم عن إدراك الحقائق العقلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opponents tried to refute the messengers by arguing that they were merely human like everyone else; the messengers accepted the likeness but answered that God grants prophethood as a special favor.
rows.anchor: فتارة حاول الناس إبطال دعواهم بالحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers concede their human likeness but say that God bestows prophethood on whomever He wills; a special divine favor does not negate shared humanity.
rows.anchor: قالت لهم رسلهم إن نحن إلا بشر مثلكم ولكن الله يمن على من يشآء من عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For God’s oneness, the messengers argue by asking whether anyone doubts God, creator of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: قالت رسلهم أفي الله شك فاطر السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For resurrection, the Qur’an argues that creation was not made in vain and asks whether the righteous should be treated like corrupt people.
rows.anchor: ما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما باطلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miracles establish the messenger’s claim to have received revelation, rather than proving rationally accessible doctrines such as monotheism and resurrection.
rows.anchor: وإنما سئل الرسل المعجزة وأتوا بها لإثبات رسالتهم وتحقيق دعواها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation is a hidden, extraordinary perception unfamiliar to ordinary people; the prophet’s claim requires showing that this special beyond-nature faculty is real.
rows.anchor: وهذا شيء خارق للعادة في نفسه من غير سنخ الإدراكات الظاهرة والباطنة التي يعرفها عامة الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection asks why the reminder was revealed to Muhammad rather than to the objectors themselves.
rows.anchor: أأنزل عليه الذكر من بيننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another objection asks why the Qur’an was not sent down on a socially eminent man from one of the two towns.
rows.anchor: لولا أنزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Critics infer that a messenger should not be a human like them and object to his ordinary eating and market-going; they demand an angel, treasure, or a garden instead.
rows.anchor: وجه الاستدلال أن دعوى الرسالة توجب أن لا يكون بشرا مثلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The critics propose an accompanying angel, a treasure, or a garden so the messenger would not need to earn his living in the markets.
rows.anchor: أو يلقى إليه كنز أو تكون له جنة يأكل منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rebuts the objection by noting that earlier messengers also ate and walked in markets, and that people test one another.
rows.anchor: وما أرسلنا قبلك من المرسلين إلا إنهم ليأكلون الطعام ويمشون في الأسواق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God sent an angel as messenger, He would make it human, which would only confuse the audience about the distinction they demanded.
rows.anchor: ولو جعلناه ملكا لجعلناه رجلا وللبسنا عليهم ما يلبسون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those demanding to witness angels or God act arrogantly; the reply says they will see angels only in a grim, final condition, as another passage likewise indicates.
rows.anchor: فذكر أنهم والحال حالهم لا يرون الملائكة إلا مع حال الموت
